headline: The Sports & Hobbies Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet teammates, count reps, pounds and miles, say how you feel, make plans, ask where things are, make polite requests and ask for help, and start Sports & Hobbies Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say sports words clearly and greet teammates, coaches and gym buddies in Spanish.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in sports words; everyday greetings

words.note: G before i or e sounds like English h: heem-NAH-syo.
Each vowel is short and clear; qu sounds like k: eh-KEE-po.
Ch sounds like ch in church.
Spanish j is a breathy h sound: HWEH-go.
Ll sounds like y in yes in most of Mexico.
Rr is a rolled, trilled r.
The accent mark shows the stressed syllable: FÚT-bol.
Stress the accented syllable: BÁS-quet-bol.
A woman coach is la entrenadora.
Very casual Mexican greeting; use it with friends, not with a coach you just met.

words.en: Nice to meet you, I'm new on the team.
words.es: Mucho gusto, soy nuevo en el equipo.
words.note: A woman says soy nueva.

words.en: Good afternoon, are you the coach?
words.note: Usted is the polite you for someone you don't know yet.

lessons.speaking: Greet a teammate at the court, say your name, say you are new on the team, and say goodbye until the next game.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say practice times, scores, sets, reps, pounds and miles with numbers up to 1,000.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and sports quantities: sets, reps, pounds, miles, laps, points

words.note: 3 series de 12 means 3 sets of 12 reps.
Also the scoreboard.
Use a las for the time something happens.
Use de before a measurement: es de 25 libras.

words.en: There are 150 of us in the league.

lessons.speaking: Tell a gym buddy what time practice is, how many sets and reps you do, and how many pounds your weight is.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say how you and your teammates feel and whether the gym, pool or a machine is free.
lessons.focus: Ser for what someone or something is, estar for a condition or location

words.note: Use estar: estoy cansado. A woman says cansada.
Estar listo means to be ready.
For a machine: está ocupada (la máquina).
A woman teammate is la compañera.
Estar: a condition that can change.
Ser: what someone is like.
In Mexico a pool is la alberca.

words.en: Carlos is injured and isn't playing today.
words.es: Carlos está lesionado y no juega hoy.

lessons.speaking: Tell a gym buddy if you are tired or ready, say who on your team is fast or strong, and ask if a machine is taken.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what gear you have, need or want, and what everyone has to do at the gym.
lessons.focus: Tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive with sports gear

words.note: Hacer pesas means to lift weights.
In Mexico sneakers are los tenis.

words.en: Do you have an extra towel?
words.note: Tienes is the tú form, fine between gym buddies.

words.es: Hay una red en la cancha 2.

words.en: Do you want to play with us?
You have to wipe down the machine afterward.
words.es: Hay que limpiar la máquina después.
words.note: Hay que + infinitive: what everyone has to do.

words.en: You have to wear a helmet on the bike.
words.es: Hay que usar casco en la bici.

lessons.speaking: Tell a gym buddy what gear you have and what you need, ask if they want to play, and say what everyone has to do after using a machine.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Make plans for games, hikes and league play and say what you can or can't do.
lessons.focus: Ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder

words.note: Partido is a game played against another team.
Short for la bicicleta; very common.

words.en: I go to the gym after work.
words.es: Voy al gimnasio después del trabajo.
words.note: A + el becomes al.

words.en: Are you going on the hike Saturday?
words.es: ¿Vas a ir a la caminata el sábado?

words.en: We're going to play a game on Sunday.
words.es: Vamos a jugar un partido el domingo.

words.en: Can you play in the league this year?
words.es: ¿Puedes jugar en la liga este año?

words.en: I can't today, how about tomorrow?

lessons.speaking: Plan a weekend activity with a friend: say where you are going, what you are going to do, and ask if they can come.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about your routine: when you train, run, swim and stretch, and what body part you work.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: In the gym people say entrenar pierna (singular) for leg day.

words.en: Do you run in the morning or the afternoon?
words.es: ¿Corres en la mañana o en la tarde?

words.en: They hike up the hill every Saturday.
words.es: Ellos suben el cerro cada sábado.

words.note: Usted takes the same verb form as él and ella.

words.en: I always stretch my back afterward.

lessons.speaking: Tell a gym buddy what you train each day, ask when they run or swim, and say what you always stretch after a workout.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask where things are, who the captain is, when games are and what the score is.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: ¿Cuántos? (plural) means how many: ¿cuántos puntos?
Written as two words in questions; porque (one word) means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? for 'what is' when asking for one choice or a name.
In Mexico showers are las regaderas.
A woman captain is la capitana.

lessons.speaking: Ask a new club teammate where the locker rooms are, who the captain is, and when the next game is.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never and not yet, and ask for more, less or another set during a workout.
lessons.focus: No, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: Never put un before it: otra serie, otro balón.
Feminine noun that takes el: el agua fría.

words.en: I don't want more weight, thanks.
I never run without warming up.

words.es: No hay nadie en la cancha 3.
words.note: Spanish uses a double negative: no hay nadie.

words.en: I'm not done with my set yet.
I want another set, but with less weight.
words.es: Quiero otra serie, pero con menos peso.

lessons.speaking: Tell a gym buddy you are not done yet, ask for another set with less weight, and say you never skip your warm-up.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask a coach or staff member for help politely and give simple polite instructions at the gym.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede...? requests and usted commands for everyday verbs

words.note: The bench press is el press de banca.

words.en: Can you help me with the bar, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede ayudar con la barra, por favor?
words.note: Puede is the polite usted form, good for a coach or staff.

words.en: Please wipe down the bench afterward.
words.es: Limpie el banco después, por favor.

words.en: Can you time it with the stopwatch?
words.es: ¿Puede tomar el tiempo con el cronómetro?

lessons.speaking: Ask a coach politely to help you with the bar and to time your set, then ask another person to wait their turn.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Spot sports words you already know and ask for help, repeats or slower Spanish at the gym.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, plus survival phrases for getting help

words.note: Words ending in -ción are feminine and match English -tion.
Words ending in -dad are feminine and match English -ty.
-ente often matches English -ent.

words.en: I don't understand, can you repeat that?
How do you say "spot" in Spanish?
I need help, my knee hurts.
words.es: Necesito ayuda, me duele la rodilla.

words.note: Llamen is the ustedes command, for everyone nearby.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate you don't understand, ask them to speak more slowly, and ask how to say a sports word in Spanish.
